newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Deutsche Telekom eases.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Deutsche Telekom eases.

text.p: Germany's state telephone company Deutsche Telekom eased on Tuesday from its strong debut as an American Depositary Receipt (ADR).
The ADRs fell 1/4 to 21-1/4 after being the target of a Monday stampede by investors wanting in on the first stage of the company's privatization.
The stock was among the most heavily traded on the New York Stock Exchange, with 6.5 million trading hands.
Andrew Melinek, head of ADR sales and research at NatWest Securities, said brokers were starting to shift their telecommunications portfolios after the Deutsche Telekom offering.
"By and large there has been a bit of repositioning of some portfolios here," he said. "People are a bit more selective about investing right now."
Britain's mobile telephone company Vodafone Group Plc rose 2-3/8 to 42-7/8 after it posted a 21 percent rise in first-half profits.
Russia's mobile telephone company Vimpel-Communications also rose 1-7/8 to 32-7/8 in a follow-on to its strong initial public offering last week.

British Petroleum Plc rose 3/4 to a year-high of 137-5/8 boosted by strong two-way trade and a recent visit to the United States by chief executive John Browne, which included meetings with American investors.
In late afternoon, advances led declines by a 283-265 margin among an 807-ADR index. Volume was 60 million shares.
